---
title: "Layers & Stack"
sidebar: get-started
---

OrcaPen separates XY layer names from physical height, material, display, and
connectivity. Use the layer map to identify polygons, then select the stack that
matches a single die or a two-die flip-chip assembly.

## Four technology definitions

| Definition | What it defines |
| --- | --- |
| `LAYER` (also `L`) | Named GDS `(layer, datatype)` pairs in `LayerMapOrpenSCPDK`. A pair identifies XY geometry; it does not assign height or material. |
| `LAYER_STACK` | Physical `LayerLevel` records: source geometry, `zmin`, thickness, material, and level-specific simulation metadata. M1 uses derived geometry rather than one raw polygon layer. |
| `LAYER_VIEWS` | Display groups, colors, hatching, and visibility from `layers.yaml`. Display settings do not change physical geometry. |
| `LAYER_CONNECTIVITY` | Declared layer-to-layer connections through TSVs, bumps, and airbridges. This is separate from a component's selected nets and terminals. |

The existing LayerViews display groups are `Metal`, `Airbridge`, `Junction`,
`DesignIntent`, `Integration`, `Alignment`, `Admin`, `gdsfactory`, and
`Simulation`. The tables below organize those layers by purpose; group names
control their display organization, not their physical material.

The complete definitions are in
[technology source](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/c4dbf7a88166f5817ffbac5fc4182a7a429ae69b/orcapen_sc_pdk/tech.py)
and [layer views](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/c4dbf7a88166f5817ffbac5fc4182a7a429ae69b/orcapen_sc_pdk/layers.yaml).
All coordinates and thicknesses below are in micrometres (µm); layer pairs are
written as `(layer, datatype)`.

## Dies, faces, and the Z frame

`D0` and `D1` identify the lower and upper dies. `TOP` and `BOTTOM` are their
faces in the common stack frame. The default stack places the D0 top substrate
face at `z = 0`; this is its chosen origin, not a required origin for every stack.

| Face prefix | Substrate face Z | Outward direction | Position in the assembly |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `D0_BOTTOM` | −500 | −Z | Lower exterior face |
| `D0_TOP` | 0 | +Z | Lower face of the interdie gap |
| `D1_BOTTOM` | 8.2 | −Z | Upper face of the interdie gap |
| `D1_TOP` | 508.2 | +Z | Upper exterior face |

For the current default M1 levels, offset is zero and thickness is 0.1 µm.
TOP metal extends toward +Z from its substrate face; BOTTOM metal extends
toward −Z.

| M1 level | Face Z (µm) | Offset (µm) | Thickness (µm) | Lower to upper Z (µm) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `D0_BOTTOM_M1` | −500 | 0 | 0.1 | −500.1 to −500 |
| `D0_TOP_M1` | 0 | 0 | 0.1 | 0 to 0.1 |
| `D1_BOTTOM_M1` | 8.2 | 0 | 0.1 | 8.1 to 8.2 |
| `D1_TOP_M1` | 508.2 | 0 | 0.1 | 508.2 to 508.3 |

The facing M1 surfaces are at `z = 0.1` and `z = 8.1`: an 8 µm metal-to-metal
gap within an 8.2 µm substrate-face separation.

## Complete layer map

### Face M1 geometry

Append each column's suffix to the row prefix to obtain the exact layer name;
for example, `D0_TOP` + `_M1_DRAW` is `LAYER.D0_TOP_M1_DRAW`.

| Prefix | `_M1_DRAW` | `_M1_ETCH` | `_M1_DOMAIN` | `_GROUND_MASK` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `D0_BOTTOM` | `(3, 0)` | `(3, 1)` | `(200, 0)` | `(111, 0)` |
| `D0_TOP` | `(1, 0)` | `(1, 1)` | `(200, 1)` | `(110, 0)` |
| `D1_BOTTOM` | `(2, 0)` | `(2, 1)` | `(200, 2)` | `(110, 1)` |
| `D1_TOP` | `(4, 0)` | `(4, 1)` | `(200, 3)` | `(111, 1)` |

These four source layers feed a face's M1 geometry; they are not four separate
physical films. The physical stack level is named `<prefix>_M1`.

Three related operations have different purposes:

| Operation | Definition and use |
| --- | --- |
| Stack-derived M1 | `M1_DOMAIN − (M1_ETCH − M1_DRAW)`. The domain bounds the metal; DRAW protects positive metal from removal by ETCH. Its derived output pair is the face's M1 DRAW pair. |
| Layout etch helper | `add_etch_for_component()` returns a copy with `M1_ETCH = GROUND_MASK − M1_DRAW`. Its default layers are D0 TOP; callers can select another face's three layers. The helper derives an etch mask, not a stack or material. |
| Component face-ground-mask route | D0 TOP and D1 BOTTOM M1 declare `geometry_source="die_face_minus_ground_mask"`, with bounds from `D0_SUBSTRATE` and `D1_SUBSTRATE`, respectively. Component simulation uses that declared face/ground-mask recipe and the component's net/terminal annotations, rather than treating each mask polygon as a conductor. |

The [etch helper source](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/c4dbf7a88166f5817ffbac5fc4182a7a429ae69b/orcapen_sc_pdk/helpers/layout/etch.py)
defines the second operation. A GROUND_MASK is an XY construction input, not
another metal level or a net named Ground.

### Other face-specific layers

The same prefix rule gives every exact name in this table.

| Prefix | `_AB_DRAW` | `_AB_VIA` | `_JJ_DRAW` | `_ALN` | `_SIM_BOUNDARY` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `D0_BOTTOM` | `(12, 0)` | `(12, 1)` | `(20, 0)` | `(81, 0)` | `(202, 0)` |
| `D0_TOP` | `(10, 0)` | `(10, 1)` | `(21, 0)` | `(80, 0)` | `(202, 1)` |
| `D1_BOTTOM` | `(11, 0)` | `(11, 1)` | `(22, 0)` | `(83, 0)` | `(202, 2)` |
| `D1_TOP` | `(13, 0)` | `(13, 1)` | `(23, 0)` | `(82, 0)` | `(202, 3)` |

| Layer family | Physical stack level |
| --- | --- |
| `<prefix>_AB_DRAW` | `<prefix>_AIRBRIDGE`: elevated Al deck. |
| `<prefix>_AB_VIA` | `<prefix>_AIRBRIDGE_VIA`: finite Al posts. |
| `<prefix>_JJ_DRAW` | None. Junction drawing layers have no declared stack thickness or material. |
| `<prefix>_ALN` | None. These are alignment layers, not a declared AlN material film. |
| `<prefix>_SIM_BOUNDARY` | Same-named zero-thickness vacuum locator sheet, not metal or an automatically assigned solver boundary. |

### Integration

The `Integration` display group contains the TSV and die-to-die contact layers.

| Exact layer name | Pair | Physical stack level or purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `D0_TOP_TSV` | `(31, 0)` | Same-named TiN through-D0 level. |
| `D1_BOTTOM_TSV` | `(31, 1)` | Same-named TiN through-D1 level. |
| `D0_D1_INDIUM_BUMP` | `(40, 0)` | Same-named finite In bump body. |
| `D0_D1_UNDER_BUMP` | `(40, 1)` | Same-named In under-bump metallization (UBM) level; excluded from simulation. |
| `D1_D2_INDIUM_BUMP` | `(41, 0)` | Mapping only; no physical level. |
| `D1_D2_UNDER_BUMP` | `(41, 1)` | Mapping only; no physical level. |

The D1–D2 bump names reserve layer pairs; this stack defines no D2 substrate,
faces, or interdie volume.

### Design intent

The `DesignIntent` display group contains these three keepouts and the four
face-specific [GROUND_MASK layers](#face-m1-geometry) listed above. These are
construction and placement inputs, not additional physical levels.

| Exact layer name | Pair | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DEVICE_KEEPOUT` | `(120, 0)` | No physical level; routing and ground-bump-fill exclusion. |
| `ROUTING_KEEPOUT` | `(120, 1)` | No physical level; routing exclusion. |
| `D0_D1_INDIUM_GROUND_KEEPOUT` | `(120, 2)` | No physical level; ground-bump-fill exclusion. |

### Simulation regions

The `Simulation` display group contains these four area layers, the four
[M1_DOMAIN layers](#face-m1-geometry), and the four
[SIM_BOUNDARY locators](#other-face-specific-layers). Their physical levels are
defined in the stack tables below.

| Exact layer name | Pair | Physical stack level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `D0_SUBSTRATE_AREA` | `(201, 0)` | XY footprint for `D0_SUBSTRATE`. |
| `D0_TO_D1_GAP_AREA` | `(201, 1)` | XY footprint for `D0_TO_D1_GAP`. |
| `D1_SUBSTRATE_AREA` | `(201, 2)` | XY footprint for `D1_SUBSTRATE`. |
| `OUTER_VACUUM_AREA` | `(201, 3)` | XY footprint for `OUTER_VACUUM`. |

### Admin

The `Admin` display group contains dicing, annotation, and error-path layers.

| Exact layer name | Pair | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DICE` | `(70, 0)` | No physical level; dicing layout. |
| `TEXT` | `(90, 0)` | No physical level; annotation. |
| `ERROR_PATH` | `(1000, 0)` | No physical level; error-path display. |

### GDSFactory utility

The `gdsfactory` display group contains settings and instance labels plus the
hidden `WG` utility layer.

| Exact layer name | Pair | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LABEL_SETTINGS` | `(100, 0)` | No physical level; GDSFactory settings labels. |
| `LABEL_INSTANCE` | `(101, 0)` | No physical level; GDSFactory instance labels. |
| `WG` | `(102, 0)` | No physical level; GDSFactory utility layer, hidden in the layer views. |

## Complete physical stack

`get_layer_stack()` and `get_two_die_flip_chip_layer_stack()` provide the full
stack below. Z intervals run from `zmin` to `zmin + thickness`; a locator's
interval collapses to a plane. These are nominal PDK dimensions.

### Substrates and vacuum regions

| Stack level | Z interval (µm) | Thickness (µm) | Material |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| `D0_SUBSTRATE` | −500 to 0 | 500 | `Si` |
| `D0_TO_D1_GAP` | 0 to 8.2 | 8.2 | `vacuum` |
| `D1_SUBSTRATE` | 8.2 to 508.2 | 500 | `Si` |
| `OUTER_VACUUM` | 508.2 to 1508.2 | 1000 | `vacuum` |

The substrates and gap declare `simulation_role="solution_region"` and
`include_in_component_simulation=True`. `OUTER_VACUUM` is marked `is_airbox=True`
but `include_in_component_simulation=False`; its named level is not a complete
surrounding simulation envelope.

### Face metal, airbridges, and locator sheets

Each row prefix expands to four exact stack names using the column suffixes.
M1 is 0.1 µm Al; airbridge posts are 3 µm Al; airbridge decks are 0.3 µm Al.
SIM_BOUNDARY is a zero-thickness `vacuum` sheet.

| Prefix | `_M1` Z interval | `_AIRBRIDGE_VIA` Z interval | `_AIRBRIDGE` Z interval | `_SIM_BOUNDARY` Z plane |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `D0_BOTTOM` | −500.1 to −500 | −503.1 to −500.1 | −503.4 to −503.1 | −500.05 |
| `D0_TOP` | 0 to 0.1 | 0.1 to 3.1 | 3.1 to 3.4 | 0.05 |
| `D1_BOTTOM` | 8.1 to 8.2 | 5.1 to 8.1 | 4.8 to 5.1 | 8.15 |
| `D1_TOP` | 508.2 to 508.3 | 508.3 to 511.3 | 511.3 to 511.6 | 508.25 |

Airbridge posts start at the outer M1 surface; the deck begins 3 µm beyond that
surface. This is a nominal rectangular post/deck model, not a reflow arch.
All four faces' airbridge levels explicitly declare conductor roles.

D0 TOP and D1 BOTTOM M1 also declare conductor roles and the face-ground-mask
recipe above. D0 BOTTOM and D1 TOP M1 have physical Al levels and derived geometry,
but their current metadata does not declare `simulation_role`; the four M1 faces
therefore do not carry identical component-simulation metadata.

The SIM_BOUNDARY sheets sit at each M1 film's midplane. They locate a sheet for
component-level terminal or boundary selection; excitation and circuit elements
are chosen by the simulation problem.

### TSVs and die-to-die contacts

| Stack level | Z interval (µm) | Thickness (µm) | Material | Physical meaning |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `D0_TOP_TSV` | −500 to 0 | 500 | `TiN` | Finite through-substrate solid; contacts `D0_BOTTOM_M1` and `D0_TOP_M1`. |
| `D1_BOTTOM_TSV` | 8.2 to 508.2 | 500 | `TiN` | Finite through-substrate solid; contacts `D1_BOTTOM_M1` and `D1_TOP_M1`. |
| `D0_D1_INDIUM_BUMP` | 0.1 to 8.1 | 8 | `In` | Finite conductor between the facing metal surfaces. |
| `D0_D1_UNDER_BUMP` | 0 to 0.1 | 0.1 | `In` | UBM source level with `exclude_from_simulation=True`; omitted from the simulation geometry. |

The public ground-bump-fill specification uses a centered 20 × 20 µm bump body
and 40 × 40 µm contact footprint, with lattice origin `(0, 0)`. Its keepout
classes are listed in the layer map above; the component selects placement.

## Select a stack

| Getter | Returned levels |
| --- | --- |
| `get_layer_stack()` | Full two-die stack: all 24 levels listed above. |
| `get_two_die_flip_chip_layer_stack()` | The full `LAYER_STACK`. |
| `get_single_die_layer_stack()` | Detached copies of `D0_SUBSTRATE`, `D0_TOP_M1`, and `D0_TOP_SIM_BOUNDARY`. This is the default single-die selection. |
| `get_single_die_layer_stack(include_airbridges=True)` | The three single-die levels plus `D0_TOP_AIRBRIDGE_VIA` and `D0_TOP_AIRBRIDGE`. |

The single-die getter removes the top M1 interdie host-void reference. It retains
the PDK's physical dimensions and materials, without an upper die or interdie
cavity; SCGSim supplies the surrounding vacuum envelope for that model.

## Declared layer connectivity

Each tuple in `LAYER_CONNECTIVITY` names a first conductor layer, a connecting
layer, and a second conductor layer. These are the five declared connections:

| First layer | Connecting layer | Second layer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `D0_BOTTOM_M1_DRAW` | `D0_TOP_TSV` | `D0_TOP_M1_DRAW` |
| `D1_BOTTOM_M1_DRAW` | `D1_BOTTOM_TSV` | `D1_TOP_M1_DRAW` |
| `D0_TOP_M1_DRAW` | `D0_D1_INDIUM_BUMP` | `D1_BOTTOM_M1_DRAW` |
| `D0_TOP_M1_DRAW` | `D0_TOP_AB_DRAW` | `D0_TOP_M1_DRAW` |
| `D1_BOTTOM_M1_DRAW` | `D1_BOTTOM_AB_DRAW` | `D1_BOTTOM_M1_DRAW` |

Physical airbridge levels exist on all four faces; the connectivity list includes
airbridge entries only for D0 TOP and D1 BOTTOM.
